t:
(a) 
Section 111(a) of the Demonstration Cities and Metropolitan Development Act of 1966 is amended—

        (1) 
by striking out “and” the third time it appears,; and
 
        (2) 
by inserting before the period at the end thereof “, and not to exceed $12,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1969”.
  
    (b) 
Section 111(b) of such Act is amended—

        (1) 
by striking out “and” the third time it appears; and
 
        (2) 
by inserting before the period at the end thereof “, and not to exceed $1,000,(W0,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1970”.
  
    (c) 
Section 111(c) of such Act is amended to read as follows:

“(c) 
Any amounts appropriated under this section shall remain available until expended, and any amounts authorized for any fiscal year under this section but not appropriated may be appropriated for any succeeding fiscal year commencing prior to July 1, 1970.”

fable.w: This section only amends appropriation authorization amounts and their availability for the Demonstration Cities and Metropolitan Development Act. The tempting reading is that the Demonstration Cities (Model Cities) program is known for citizen participation, but the name of the Act is not a participation process. Nothing in this text requires consultation, hearings, rulemaking, advisory bodies, or rights to sue involving parties outside the federal government.
fable.s: Any amounts appropriated under this section shall remain available until expended

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to appropriation limits and availability of funds within the Demonstration Cities and Metropolitan Development Act. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The text deals solely with internal federal budgetary mechanics.
qwen_block.s: Section 111(a) of the Demonstration Cities and Metropolitan Development Act of 1966 is amended— (1) by striking out “and” the third time it appears,; and (2) by inserting before the period at the end thereof “, and not to exceed $12,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1969”.

opus.w: This provision only changes appropriation limits and says how long the funds stay available. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue that involves outside parties. The mention of cities and metropolitan development is only in the Act's title and is not an actual outside-party process.
opus.s: Any amounts appropriated under this section shall remain available until expended
opus.b: This section only changes appropriation authorizations for the Demonstration Cities program. The name "Demonstration Cities and Metropolitan Development Act" might suggest a city or local role, but that is just the Act's title. Nothing in the text sets up any process where people outside the federal government take part in a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section solely concerns the authorization and availability of federal appropriations for specific fiscal years. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with parties outside the federal government, such as states, local governments, or the public. The text is purely administrative regarding budgetary funds.
qwen_chat.s: Any amounts appropriated under this section shall remain available until expended, and any amounts authorized for any fiscal year under this section but not appropriated may be appropriated for any succeeding fiscal year commencing prior to July 1, 1970.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because this section amends a broader Act (Demonstration Cities and Metropolitan Development Act), it implicitly includes participation mechanisms from that Act. However, the definition requires the *section itself* to involve participation. This specific text only deals with appropriation amounts and fiscal year availability. It contains no language regarding consultation, public comment, advisory boards with outside members, or coordination with non-federal entities.
